newsitem.title: JAPAN: Racketeer admits deals with Daiwa, Nikko--Jiji.
newsitem.headline: Racketeer admits deals with Daiwa, Nikko--Jiji.

text.p: Corporate racketeer Ryuichi Koike has told prosecutors that Nikko Securities Co Ltd and Daiwa Securities Co Ltd conducted illegal stock deals for him, Jiji news agency said on Monday.
Koike is a key figure in the high-profile payoff scandal involving Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd and Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
The Jiji report quoted a lawyer for Koike as saying that Nikko and Daiwa, two other leading Japanese brokerages, had also conducted illegal deals for him.
Nikko and Daiwa said they could not immediately comment on the report.
"All of our spokesmen are out for lunch so we cannot comment on the Jiji report," a Daiwa official said.
"We cannot comment right now as we don't know about the Jiji report yet," a Nikko spokesman said, adding that he would check whether the report was true or not.
The president of Nikko Securities, Kichiro Takao, told the firm's annual shareholders' meeting on Friday that he was not aware of any illegal payments by the firm to shareholders.
A Daiwa Securities spokesman later told Reuters that the securities house had not had time to study the Jiji report so could not comment on it.
"We have not studied the contents of the report, so we would like to refrain from making comment," the spokesman said.
Jiji also reported that Japan's securities watchdog had already begun a full-scale investigation into the two brokerages. Both are among Japan's "Big Four" brokerages, along with Nomura.
An official at Japan's Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) had no comment on the Jiji report.
